title: A protected-folder guard must also protect a folder that holds a protected root
rule: When a folder (a source root, the library folder, a system font folder) can be kept but never removed as a whole, check the side that would be removed for three things: it is the protected folder, it lies inside one, or it holds one. Sources can nest, because add_source accepts a parent of an existing source, so a folder below one source root can be another root. Anything that rolls folders up to their parents (climbing a contained pair, summing a tree) must stop at a root and never report a parent that hides it. Test it with a root nested inside another source: one test where the parent is the removed side and is refused, and one where the nested root is the kept side and is allowed.
rationale: E56.6 (#666): the protection matched roots only by equality and the climb went past any folder under a root. A library folder nested in a watched source climbed to its parent, lost its protected mark, and the folder-pair plan would have removed its files.
